verdicts.originalText: Base plungeFrames = after Press E (plungePressFrames in gcsim; hitmark=36f). plungeVariants["After Hold E"] = plungeHoldFrames (hitmark=41f). Variant is auto-selected by the parser based on which E token preceded P in the rotation string.
verdicts.rationale: This is the exact caveat the style guide lists as its Delete worked example. Every sentence is either curator-facing internals (gcsim field names, hitmark frame counts) or a description of working behavior (plunge-variant auto-selection is on the CAN list and wired end-to-end). It states no timeline divergence or omission, so a player who knows the character would not be misled without it. Remove the caveat key; demote the source detail to _curatorNotes.

demotedNotes: Base plungeFrames represent the Press-E plunge path (plungePressFrames in gcsim, hitmark 36f); the 'After Hold E' plungeVariant represents plungeHoldFrames (hitmark 41f). The plunge variant is auto-selected from whichever E token (Press vs Hold) preceded P in the notation string.

verdicts.originalText: Frames reflect the standard (no glide cancel) path. Glide-cancel path (common for E→Q/swap in practice): swap=60, Q=61, D=61, J=59 — not modelled as a separate variant.
verdicts.proposedText: Shown timing assumes a standard cast; glide-canceling into the burst or a swap (common in practice) is faster and is not modeled.
verdicts.rationale: Legitimate divergence: the timeline shows the standard no-glide-cancel cast timing, but the widely-used glide-cancel path is faster and isn't authored as a variant. Kept as a caveat because it's a real data-authoring gap, not auto-modelable. Compression drops the raw frame values (banned curator-speak) and fixes the double-L 'modelled' to 'modeled'. 'The burst' is a kind-only same-character reference, allowed. 'Faster' is traceable to the caveat's own numbers (glide-cancel swap 60 < base swap 77).
